newsitem.title: TURKEY: World Bank plans $1.5 bln aid to Turkey over 3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: World Bank plans $1.5 bln aid to Turkey over 3 yrs.

text.p: The World Bank is planning to provide Turkey with a financial assistance programme worth up to $1.5 billion over three years, an official from the bank said on Friday.
"What we are proposing is to lend up to $1.5 billion over a three-year period," Johannes Linn, vice president for Europe and Central Asia at the World Bank, told a news conference.
He said the programme, which would be worth about $500 million a year in project commitments, is expected to be approved by the bank's board in September.

The aid, part of the bank's 'country assistance strategy', will include programmes in education and health, with greater attention to lesser developed regions, Linn said. The bank will also provide assistance in the fields of farm development, urban infrastructure and social services, irrigation and technology development.

Linn said the aid over the coming years could be higher if the new secularist government made progress in key economic reforms. "Our headroom is not exhausted by the $1.5 billion over three years," he said.
But he said further aid, potentially as high as $5 billion, would only be considered with support from the International Monetary Fund.
Linn was speaking at the end of a three-day visit to Turkey with Ajay Chhibber, director of the World Bank's Turkey programme.
They met Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz, senior ministers and officials from the treasury, finance ministry and state planning organisation.
The World Bank officials recommended a series of measures to the new government, established at the end of June to replace the previous Islamist-led coalition.
The officials proposed government action in areas such as fiscal stabilisation, continued privatisation, social security reform and rationalising agricultural incentives.
